(1) the context representation has an impact on the performance of the learned word embeddings, and (2) the context representation is task dependent.
(1) for most tasks, the context types of word embeddings are not sensitive, and (2) the representations of context are sensitive.
the context types that are most helpful in learning word embeddings are: 1) syntactic context; 2) semantic context.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best context type and representation for learning word embeddings are task-specific and dataset-specific.
(1) for the tasks of word similarity, word analogy, and word classification, the best context type for learning word embeddings is the window context.
(1) the most important factor is the type of context (e.g. left or right context), not the representation (e.g. bag-of-words or character n-gram) or the size (e.g. 5 or 10).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the context should be defined by a word sequence, and the representation of context should be a bag of words, or a word sequence, instead of a word vector.
the best context is the one that is most related to the target words.
we need to consider the following aspects when designing word embedding models: (1) context selection, (2) representation of contexts, (3) learning objective and (4) the combination of the above.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best context type and representation for a specific task are different.
the best context type for a specific task depends on the characteristics of the task and the data.
the context representation should be carefully designed for each task.
